newsitem.title: USA: Golfer Norman feels guilty about Clinton tumble.
newsitem.headline: Golfer Norman feels guilty about Clinton tumble.

text.p: Australian golfer Greg Norman said on Tuesday he felt guilty and emotionally drained because President Bill Clinton tumbled down steps at the pro's home in Florida and was injured.
Norman said in his first interview about the misstep that there was nothing he could do about the accident at his Hobe Sound ocean front home early on Friday morning.
"He just took a misstep, it is as simple as that," Norman said on CNN.

The fall required Clinton to be rushed back to Washington where he underwent surgery for a torn right knee tendon, an operation that will require him to use crutches for up to eight weeks and exercise for months to regain strength in his leg.

"How you handle it is pretty tough," said a subdued Norman, "mainly because of the fact that if you were staying at my house and you fell down and you put a cast on your leg, I'd be devastated for you."
"But now you're talking about the president of the United States -- it's even harder to accept that," he added.

He said he and his wife have sat down since the incident and reflected that "there was nothing we could have done -- it wasn't our fault but you feel guilty, you feel the emotional draining of it all."
